newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Renong stock down on steel firm concern.
newsitem.headline: Renong stock down on steel firm concern.

text.p: Shares of Malaysian conglomerate Renong Bhd were down on Monday on concerns it may go through with a speculated purchase of a 69.2 percent stake in Philippines-based National Steel Corp (NSC), dealers said.
"The steel operation is loss-making," said an institutional dealer. He estimated that the purchase could be funded by a two billion ringgit rights issue by Renong, which would cause dilution.
Officials at Renong did not immediately have a comment, and NSC officials declined comment. Renong's stock ended the morning down 14 cents to 4.52 ringgit.
Earlier on Monday, Hong Kong-based Hottic Investments Ltd said it has formally acquired 82.5 percent of NSC with the payment of $800 million to Malaysian firm Wing Tiek Holdings Bhd .
"It's a big question mark, and that's why people are selling it (Renong's stock) down," said an equity analyst referring to the rumoured NSC buy by Renong.

But she said she did not believe Renong would pay more than the 1.2 billion ringgit Wing Tiek sold the NSC stake for. Weak steel prices in 1996 accounted for NSC's losses, she added. "If NSC becomes profitable, it won't be that bad of a deal."
